about.title: About Vesign
about.intro: Vesign is an investment research platform that monitors the US stock market every trading day, automatically identifying high-conviction buy and sell opportunities through a multi-layered analysis of market conditions and company fundamentals.
about.feature1Desc: Every trading day, Vesign scans thousands of stocks and surfaces candidates that meet strict entry and exit criteria — so you never miss an opportunity.
about.feature2Desc: Track your holdings across multiple watchlists, monitor your P&L in real time, and compare your portfolio performance against Vesign's signals over time.
about.feature3Desc: A complete log of every signal-driven trade with win rates, average yields, and holding periods — so you can evaluate past performance at a glance.
about.howDesc: Vesign evaluates stocks across multiple dimensions simultaneously: price action, market sentiment, company financial health, and analyst consensus. Only stocks that meet all criteria at once are surfaced — keeping the signal list focused and actionable.
about.disclaimer: Vesign is a research and decision-support tool only. It does not constitute financial advice, and nothing on this platform should be interpreted as a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Vesign bears no responsibility for any investment decisions made by users based on the information or signals provided. Past signal performance is not indicative of future results. Always conduct your own due diligence and consult a qualified financial advisor before investing.

ld.faq.title: Answered straight
ld.faq.items.advice.a: No. VeSign is a research and information platform. Signals are the output of a systematic model and are published for research purposes only — they are not personalized investment advice, and we are not a broker or advisor. Always do your own diligence.
ld.faq.items.howGenerated.a: A daily systematic process screens 1,800+ US-listed stocks and combines technical indicators, a machine-learning price model, analyst consensus, and company financial health into a single decision. When the evidence lines up, a BUY or SELL is published — with the reasoning written out in plain language.
ld.faq.items.performanceSource.q: Where do the performance numbers come from?
ld.faq.items.performanceSource.a: They are the results of running the model’s strategy on historical US market data. The full list of trades the model generated — entries, exits, winners and losers — is published on the performance page, alongside an equity curve against the S&P 500. They are not live-traded or real-money returns, and past performance does not guarantee future results.
ld.faq.items.dataSource.q: Where does the data come from?
ld.faq.items.dataSource.a: Prices, fundamentals, and analyst estimates come from institutional-grade market data providers and are refreshed daily after the US close. Some displayed prices may be delayed or indicative.
ld.faq.items.freePlan.a: Yes. The Free plan includes the market overview, a sample of the daily signals, and the full public track record — no credit card required.
